result.topic_en: Notes on the case where a theta-type function $\vartheta(r_1, r_2, \dots, r_p)$ vanishes: points $\eta$ are determined so that the argument system is congruent to sums of values $\alpha$, together with a remark on the vanishing of the first $m$ derivatives and the resulting freedom in choosing the points.

items.english: If the first m derivatives of the function $\vartheta$ at $v = r$ all vanish but the (m+1)-th do not all vanish, then m of the points can be chosen [freely] and thereby the rest are determined, and conversely.
